blocker.summary: r475 disproves r473/r474's 'silent plateau' reading of the native probe. A live trace (30s window) shows 36 draws before the diagnostic capture snapshot and 50 MORE afterward (including a batch that triggers r459's MSAA codepath, sample_count=4) -- the GPU/VD thread keeps processing real content well past the point r473/r474 read as a stall; the probe window is just a fixed-time snapshot, not a completion signal. The real reason the capture stays black: all 86 draws across the whole run are vertex_count=1/index_count=1 (auto-indexed, single-vertex -- consistent with early boot/logo/title-screen UI elements, not flight-gameplay 3D geometry), and every one of the 9 rejected drain batches hits the exact same already-known 'no pinned variant matches this draw state' registry-coverage gap. This explains why r472's 320-entry registry (built from r470's flight-gameplay oracle route) had zero effect on the native probe: the early content it naturally reaches uses a completely different shader set than flight gameplay, never captured by any oracle run so far. No source changed this cycle (pure trace analysis). Named for r476: a new oracle campaign targeted at early boot/title-screen content (not r470's flight route) would likely capture the shaders the native probe actually needs -- the most direct path to native visible content, but substantial new work (repeating r463-r472 for a different route), not a decision to take unilaterally given the oracle budget already spent this campaign. Still open, non-blocking: decode fetch_const[1]'s repeated pattern to confirm the 'textured UI element' hypothesis; the native backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438/r454-r474).
